He walked down to the landing anyway. Fifty years of meeting the morning boat had worn a path in him that his legs still followed, and the water did not object to an old man standing at the rail with no one to greet. What surprised him was how little the mornings changed. He had thought himself the harbormaster, the one the boat depended on. Now he understood he had mostly been its witness.
